summary_en: This phase 1 study tests CD19-specific CAR T cells, which are a patient's own T cells changed to target CD19, in people with non-Hodgkin lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia, or acute lymphocytic leukemia that has returned or has not gone away. The cells are given by infusion at stated dose levels of 1×10^6, 5×10^6, or 2×10^7 cells/m² in the dose-escalation phase, and at the maximum tolerated dose in the expansion phase; how long and how often are not stated. The study aims to find the highest safe dose and to measure how long the cells last, side effects, and whether the therapy might help.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba células T con receptor quimérico específico para CD19, que son células T propias del paciente modificadas para atacar CD19, en personas con linfoma no Hodgkin, leucemia linfocítica crónica o leucemia linfoblástica aguda que han recidivado o no han desaparecido. Las células se administran por infusión en niveles de dosis indicados de 1×10^6, 5×10^6 o 2×10^7 células/m² en la fase de escalado de dosis, y en la dosis máxima tolerada en la fase de expansión; no se indica la duración ni la frecuencia. El estudio busca encontrar la dosis más alta segura y medir cuánto tiempo duran las células, los efectos secundarios y si la terapia podría ayudar.
who_for: Recurrent B-cell lymphoma, or ALL or CLL that has come back or not gone away
Newly diagnosed ALL or CLL when standard therapy cannot be given or completed
Relapsed or refractory aggressive B-cell lymphoma with a planned high-dose therapy and stem cell transplant
Age 75 or younger; the first 3 patients must be adults 18 or older
not_for: Active infection needing antibiotics, or active HIV or HTLV infection
Other cancer history unless treated with curative intent at least 2 years before entry
Investigational agents or tumor vaccines within the previous 6 weeks
Allergy to murine (mouse) protein-containing products; pregnant or breastfeeding
Tumor location where enlargement could cause airway obstruction
